problem.name: Ordered search
problem.statement_latex: Given oracle access to a nondecreasing bit string $x_1\le\cdots\le x_n$, determine its first $1$, including the all-zero case. Complexity counts exact comparison queries.
problem.statement_text: Given oracle access to a nondecreasing bit string $x_1\le\cdots\le x_n$, determine its first $1$, including the all-zero case. Complexity counts exact comparison queries.

strength.description_latex: No established asymptotic speedup in the comparison stated above.
strength.description_text: No established asymptotic speedup in the comparison stated above.

evidence.description_latex: The leading query constant and the classical binary-search comparator are proved; both asymptotic orders are logarithmic.
evidence.description_text: The leading query constant and the classical binary-search comparator are proved; both asymptotic orders are logarithmic.

hardware.description_latex: The algorithm requires coherent input access and fault-tolerant execution of the stated procedure; its circuit and workspace requirements depend on that access implementation.
hardware.description_text: The algorithm requires coherent input access and fault-tolerant execution of the stated procedure; its circuit and workspace requirements depend on that access implementation.

quantum.headline_latex: $\ln n/\pi+o(\log n)$ exact queries by the Carolan--Childs algorithm.
quantum.headline_text: $\ln n/\pi+o(\log n)$ exact queries by the Carolan–Childs algorithm.

classical.headline_latex: $\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil$ exact queries by binary search; both bounds are $\Theta(\log n)$.
classical.headline_text: $\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil$ exact queries by binary search; both bounds are $\Theta(\log n)$.
